senses.gloss: Emanation Body [appearing as] whatever tames [whoever needs taming]
senses.context: A type of sprul sku (Emanation Body) characterized by manifesting in whatever form is required to discipline or train those to be tamed. The element gang here has its indefinite/relative force, 'whoever, whatever,' combined with 'dul 'to tame, to discipline'.
Negation of gang ba 'being full, filled'; renders Sanskrit aparipūrṇa and asampūrṇa. Used of what is not filled up or not brought to completion.
In Conze's usage ({C}) the term is glossed 'without having fulfilled', i.e. not having completed or filled out what was to be accomplished.
Future/resultative form of gang ba 'to be full, to fill'; corresponds to Sanskrit āpūryate and paripūryate, i.e. 'is filled up, becomes complete'.

gang tshun.gloss: up to the point of, as far as

senses.gloss: up to the point of, as far as
senses.context: An expression marking extent or limit, glossed 'up to the point of'. Formed with the indefinite relative gang.
Temporal relative expression corresponding to Sanskrit yadā, introducing the clause 'when...'. Built on gang plus tshe 'time'.

gang zag gang gis yid gtad pas mthong ts.gloss: phenomena naturally able to produce the thought "this and that are alike"

senses.gloss: phenomena naturally able to produce the thought "this and that are alike"
senses.context: A definitional formula for phenomena that, merely upon being seen by any person who directs the mind toward them, of their own accord give rise to an awareness thinking, "This and that are alike." The wording describes a class of objects characterized by their natural capacity to induce a judgment of similarity in an observer.

gang zag gi bdag tu 'dzin pa'i blo.gloss: awareness grasping at a self of persons

senses.gloss: awareness grasping at a self of persons
senses.context: A mind or consciousness that apprehends persons as having a self. Named as the apprehending awareness, rather than the object apprehended.

gang zag gi bdag med kyi dbang du byas p.gloss: ultimate-non-nature in terms of the selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: ultimate-non-nature in terms of the selflessness of persons
senses.context: The ultimate-non-nature (don dam pa ngo bo nyid med pa) as posited from the standpoint of, or with reference to, the selflessness of persons. The phrase 'dbang du byas pa'i' marks that this particular non-nature is being specified in relation to that selflessness.

gang zag gi bdag med rtogs pa'i rnal 'by.gloss: yogic ground of realizing the selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: yogic ground of realizing the selflessness of persons
senses.context: A level or stage of yoga (rnal 'byor gyi sa) characterized by realization of the selflessness of persons.

gang zag gi bdag med dang chos kyi bdag.gloss: thoroughly established natures in terms of the two selflessnesses

senses.gloss: thoroughly established natures in terms of the two selflessnesses
senses.context: Thoroughly established natures (yongs grub) as posited with reference to both the selflessness of persons and the selflessness of phenomena. The phrase 'dbang du byas pa'i' indicates that these thoroughly established natures are specified in relation to those two selflessnesses.

gang zag gi bdag med spyi ldog.gloss: generality-isolate of the selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: generality-isolate of the selflessness of persons
senses.context: A technical term of Tibetan epistemology/logic designating the selflessness of persons taken merely as a general isolate (spyi ldog), i.e. that object considered in isolation from its instances and from other characteristics. Rendered by Hopkins as 'generality-isolate of the selflessness of persons'.

gang zag gi bdag med phra mo'i rnam pa c.gloss: having the aspect of the subtle selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: having the aspect of the subtle selflessness of persons
senses.context: Said of a consciousness or path that bears the aspect (rnam pa) of the subtle (phra mo) selflessness of persons, as distinguished from the coarse form of that selflessness. Hopkins glosses it, as a provisional rendering, 'having the aspect of the subtle selflessness of persons'.
The grosser or less subtle level of the selflessness of persons (rags pa, 'coarse', as opposed to phra mo, 'subtle'). Used in presentations that distinguish degrees of the person's lack of self.

gang zag gi bdag 'dzin pa'i blo.gloss: awareness apprehending a self of persons

senses.gloss: awareness apprehending a self of persons
senses.context: A mind or awareness (blo) that conceives or holds (bdag 'dzin pa) a self of persons, i.e. the consciousness that is the opposite of realizing the selflessness of persons. Hopkins: 'awareness apprehending a self of persons'.

gang zag gi bye brag.gloss: instance of a person; distinction among persons

senses.gloss: instance of a person; distinction among persons
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgala-bheda (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra literature), where bheda indicates a division, differentiation, or particular case. Hopkins renders it as 'instance of a person', i.e. a particular member falling under the general category 'person'.

gang zag gi longs spyad bya.gloss: objects of use of a person; objects a person enjoys

senses.gloss: objects of use of a person; objects a person enjoys
senses.context: A compound of gang zag (person) with longs spyad bya, the objects to be used or enjoyed. It designates the things that serve as a person's articles of use or objects of enjoyment.

gang zag gi bsam pa.gloss: a person's thought; attitude of a person

senses.gloss: a person's thought; attitude of a person
senses.context: The bsam pa (thought, intention, attitude) belonging to a gang zag (person). Used where the mental attitude or way of thinking of an individual is at issue.

gang zag gi bsam pa la dgongs pa.gloss: in consideration of a person's attitude

senses.gloss: in consideration of a person's attitude
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgalāśaya-abhiprāya (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra context): the intention or purpose that takes account of a person's disposition (āśaya). It renders an expression for teaching or acting with the individual's frame of mind in view.

Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgalābhisaṃbodha: abhisaṃbodha (manifest, direct realization) with respect to the pudgala (person). It refers to realizing the person clearly and directly, rather than merely inferring or conceptualizing it.

gang zag tu smra ba.gloss: propounding a person; proponent of a person

senses.gloss: propounding a person; proponent of a person
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgalavādin, one who asserts or speaks in terms of a pudgala (person). The Tibetan can render both the act of propounding a person and the holder of such an assertion.

Renders Sanskrit pudgala-grāha: the act of grasping at or conceiving of a person (pudgala) as truly existent. Used in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra contexts for the misconception that is the object of negation in the selflessness of persons.

gang zag rtag gcig rang dbang can gyis s.gloss: a person's emptiness of being permanent, unitary, and autonomous

senses.gloss: a person's emptiness of being permanent, unitary, and autonomous
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit nityaikasvatantra-śūnyapudgala. It designates the absence, in a person, of the three qualities permanence (nitya), unitariness (eka), and autonomy (svatantra) — a coarse form of the selflessness of persons.

gang zag dang chos dag mi dmigs pa'i phy.gloss: because persons and phenomena are not apprehended

senses.gloss: because persons and phenomena are not apprehended
senses.context: Renders pudgala-dharmayor anupalambhāt, a causal clause: 'due to the non-apprehension of persons and [other] phenomena.' It states the reason or ground, namely that neither the person nor phenomena are observed or found.

gang zag dang chos med pa'i mtshan nyid.gloss: having the character of the non-existence of persons and phenomena

senses.gloss: having the character of the non-existence of persons and phenomena
senses.context: Renders pudgala-dharmābhāva-lakṣaṇatva: the state of being characterized by the absence (abhāva) of persons and of [other] phenomena.
Renders pudgala-dharma-nairātmya, the twofold absence of self: the selflessness in persons (pudgala) and the selflessness in [other] phenomena (dharma).

gang zag dang chos la bdag med pa dag yo.gloss: in order to thoroughly understand the selflessness of persons and phenomena

senses.gloss: in order to thoroughly understand the selflessness of persons and phenomena
senses.context: A purpose clause (…phyir) stating the aim of a teaching or practice: full comprehension (yongs su shes pa, parijñā) of the two selflessnesses — that of persons (gang zag gi bdag med) and that of [other] phenomena (chos kyi bdag med). Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials as pudgala-dharma-nairātmyayoḥ parijñārtham.

A person (gang zag, pudgala) qualified as dam pa, 'excellent, holy, true' (Skt. sat), i.e. a superior or saintly individual. The Sanskrit equivalent recorded from the Madhyāntavibhāga materials is uncertain (sat, perhaps sat-pudgala).

gang zag gdags pa.gloss: imputation of a person; designation as a person

senses.gloss: imputation of a person; designation as a person
senses.context: The act or fact of designating/imputing (gdags pa, prajñapti) something as a 'person' (gang zag, pudgala). Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials as pudgala-prajñapti.

gang zag bdag med gi rang ldog.gloss: self-isolate of a selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: self-isolate of a selflessness of persons
senses.context: Technical term of Tibetan logic: the rang ldog ('self-isolate') of the selflessness of persons (gang zag gi bdag med), i.e. that phenomenon considered strictly in its own right as opposed to its instances or other isolates. The comparandum supplies only the equivalent 'self-isolate of a selflessness of persons'.

gang zag bdag med rang ldog.gloss: self-isolate of the selflessness of the person

senses.gloss: self-isolate of the selflessness of the person
senses.context: Variant spelling of gang zag bdag med gi rang ldog: the selflessness of the person taken as its own isolate (rang ldog) in the terminology of Tibetan logic and 'collected topics'. The comparandum gives only this rendering, without further specification.

gang zag bdag 'dzin.gloss: conception of a self of persons

senses.gloss: conception of a self of persons
senses.context: Compound of gang zag (person) and bdag 'dzin (conception/apprehension of self); the mental holding of persons as having a self. Hopkins renders it 'conception of a self of persons'; the gloss is marked as a provisional (phrase-level) rendering.

gang zag bdag 'dzin gnyis.gloss: the two conceptions of a self of persons

senses.gloss: the two conceptions of a self of persons
senses.context: The term gang zag bdag 'dzin (conception of a self of persons) enumerated as a pair, i.e. two types of such conception. The comparanda give only the enumeration; they do not specify which two types are meant.

A phrase rendering Sanskrit kadā cit pudgalo nāsti with negation (na-), i.e. denying that there is ever a time when a person does not exist. Attested as a scriptural/commentarial statement in the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra material.

gang zag rnam par gzhig pa.gloss: disintegration of the person; destruction of the person

senses.gloss: disintegration of the person; destruction of the person
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgala-vināśa, the perishing or breaking up of the person. Formed with rnam par gzhig pa (to demolish, break down), so it may also carry the sense of analytically dismantling the person; the comparanda support only the rendering 'disintegration/destruction'.

Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgala-vyavasthāna / pudgala-vyavasthāpana, the setting forth or conventional establishing of the person. To be distinguished from the similarly spelled gang zag rnam par gzhig pa (disintegration of the person).

A compositional factor (saṃskāra) not associated with mind and not itself a person, i.e. a member of the category of non-associated compositional factors excluding persons. The Sanskrit is reconstructed as *apudgala-viprayukta-saṃskāra.

gang zag ma yin par gyur pa'i ldan min '.gloss: non-associated compositional factor which is not a person

senses.gloss: non-associated compositional factor which is not a person
senses.context: Designates those non-associated compositional factors that are not persons; an expanded form (gyur pa'i) of the same technical category. Reconstructed Sanskrit *apudgala-viprayukta-saṃskāra.

gang zag mi rtag pa nyid du thal bar 'gy.gloss: it would [absurdly] follow that persons are impermanent

senses.gloss: it would [absurdly] follow that persons are impermanent
senses.context: A consequence (thal 'gyur, prasaṅga) stated in debate: from a given position it would follow that the person is merely impermanent. Corresponds to Sanskrit pudgalasyānityatva-prasaṅgāt in the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra literature.

gang zag med pa.gloss: absence of a person; selflessness of persons

senses.gloss: absence of a person; selflessness of persons
senses.context: The non-existence of a person or personality, rendering Sanskrit niṣpudgala / niṣpudgalatva. In Conze's renderings of Perfection of Wisdom texts it appears as 'no personality' or 'without personality'.
One who asserts the existence of a person (pudgala), Sanskrit pudgalavādin. Used as a doxographical designation for holders of such a tenet.
A person (gang zag) taken as nothing more than that — the bare designation 'person' without anything further added. The qualifier tsam ('mere, only') restricts the referent to the person alone.
Rendering Sanskrit apratipudgala, a person for whom there is no counterpart or rival. Used as an epithet of one who has no match, glossed simply as 'without a match'.

gang zag yin par gyur pa'i ldan min 'du.gloss: non-associated compositional factor which is a person

senses.gloss: non-associated compositional factor which is a person
senses.context: A person considered as belonging to the category of non-associated compositional factors (ldan min 'du byed, viprayukta-saṃskāra), i.e. as a conditioned phenomenon that is neither form nor consciousness. The Sanskrit reconstruction *pudgala-viprayukta-saṃskāra reflects this classification of the person within Abhidharma-style enumerations.

gang zag yod par khas blang bar mi bya.gloss: persons are not to be asserted as existing

senses.gloss: persons are not to be asserted as existing
senses.context: A doctrinal statement (Sanskrit na vā pudgalo 'sti) denying that a person may be maintained or conceded to exist. It functions as a rejection of asserting the person's existence, rather than as a term for a thing.
Sanskrit pudgala-vādin: one who asserts, or advocates the position, that a person exists. Used as a doxographical label for holders of such a view.

gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod k.gloss: emptiness of the person as a self-sufficient substantially existent entity

senses.gloss: emptiness of the person as a self-sufficient substantially existent entity
senses.context: Names the absence, in a person (gang zag), of the mode of existence called "substantially existent" (rdzas yod) understood specifically as "self-sufficient" (rang rkya thub pa), i.e. able to stand on its own. Per the comparanda it is rendered as the emptiness of a person as being substantially existent in the sense of being self-sufficient.

gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod d.gloss: non-establishment of the person as a self-sufficient substantially existent entity

senses.gloss: non-establishment of the person as a self-sufficient substantially existent entity
senses.context: The negative formulation ma grub pa states that a person (gang zag) is not established as substantially existent (rdzas yod) in the sense of being self-sufficient (rang rkya thub pa). It is the counterpart, phrased as non-establishment rather than emptiness, of gang zag rang rkya thub pa'i rdzas yod kyis stong pa.

gang zag la mi srid snyam pa.gloss: thinking that something does not occur among persons

senses.gloss: thinking that something does not occur among persons
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit asambhāvanā pudgale, the phrase expresses the thought that some quality or event is not possible or does not occur (mi srid) in the case of persons (gang zag). Hopkins glosses it as thinking, "[Such and such] does not occur among persons."

gang yang rung ba zhig ma tshang ba.gloss: any one [of them] being incomplete or lacking

senses.gloss: any one [of them] being incomplete or lacking
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit anyatama-vaikalya, the deficiency (ma tshang ba, vaikalya) of any one member (gang yang rung ba, anyatama) of a set. Used where the absence of even a single required factor is at issue; Hopkins glosses it as "any incomplete."

gang yin pa de thams cad.gloss: all of whatever is...; all whatsoever

senses.gloss: all of whatever is...; all whatsoever
senses.context: A distributive-universal construction built on the indefinite gang ("whatever, whichever"): whatever is such-and-such, all of that. Hopkins gives "all of whatever is..." and "all whatsoever."

gang yin par 'gro.gloss: goes into whatever there is; goes as it comes

senses.gloss: goes into whatever there is; goes as it comes
senses.context: Rendering Skt. yathāgami, describing movement that follows whatever is encountered. Glossed as 'goes into ... which he comes across on his way', i.e., proceeding in accordance with whatever presents itself.

Corresponds to Skt. yac ca na vikalpayati, a relative construction: 'that with respect to which one does not conceptualize'. Used of a subject or object regarding which no conceptual differentiation (rnam par rtog pa) occurs, hence also rendered 'non-conceptual with respect to anything'.

gang las bskyod par bgyid lags.gloss: from what does one free oneself? (honorific)

senses.gloss: from what does one free oneself? (honorific)
senses.context: An honorific interrogative phrase corresponding to Skt. uccālayati, glossed 'free oneself from'. The form bgyid lags marks polite/honorific register, typical of a respectful question about that from which one is moved or released.
An indefinite-relative phrase built on gang ('which, whichever') with the plural/collective dag and the demonstrative 'di, meaning 'whichsoever of these'.

gangs can mkhas pa.gloss: scholar of the Land of Snows (Tibet)

senses.gloss: scholar of the Land of Snows (Tibet)
senses.context: Compound of gangs can, 'the Snowy (Land)', an epithet of Tibet, with mkhas pa, 'scholar, learned one'. Refers to a Tibetan scholar.

Rendered by Sanskrit karaṇḍaka and glossed 'basket' in the Perfection of Wisdom (C) materials; a container or receptacle. The alternate Sanskrit comparandum cañca points to a similar woven or plaited container.

Corresponds to Sanskrit yatreccham, 'wherever one wishes.' Used adverbially of movement or activity carried out wherever, or in whatever way, is desired; in the Perfection of Wisdom (C) context, 'wherever it wishes.'

gar yang khyab pa ni chu zla lta bu'o.gloss: pervading everywhere like a moon in water

senses.gloss: pervading everywhere like a moon in water
senses.context: A set phrase glossed 'pervading everywhere like a moon in water.' It employs the simile of the moon's reflection appearing in any body of water to illustrate all-pervasiveness.

gar log.gloss: Garlok, a small kingdom in western Tibet

senses.gloss: Garlok, a small kingdom in western Tibet
senses.context: A proper name identified as Garlok, a small kingdom in Nga-ri (mNga' ris), western Tibet.
Equated with Sanskrit turūṣka, a designation for Turkic peoples of the northwest.

gal te ... gyur.gloss: if it would be, if it were to become

senses.gloss: if it would be, if it were to become
senses.context: A conditional construction corresponding to Sanskrit ced bhavet (Madhyāntavibhāga I.21), 'if it would be.' The gal te introduces the condition and gyur supplies the hypothetical verb 'be/become.'

see_also: gal te … skyes par gyur na

senses.context: Conditional connective introducing a hypothesis, glossed by Hopkins simply as "If...". Functionally equivalent to the more common gal te, here with the locative/conditional particle na attached.

Rendered in Sanskrit as nāṭaka-itihāsa, i.e. dramatic performance together with legendary narrative; Hopkins glosses the element as "play." The Tibetan phrase joins the three items (dramatic pieces, song-texts and stories) with dang. The entry as transmitted also carries a stray gloss of the particle gi (genitive "of, by, in, which"; also non-case "and, but"), which does not belong to the phrase i

gi gu.gloss: gi gu, the vowel sign for i

senses.gloss: gi gu, the vowel sign for i
senses.context: Name of the Tibetan vowel marker written above a consonant to indicate the vowel i. As noted in the Sanskrit comparandum, long ī is written with a doubled gi gu (gi gu nyis brtsegs) over the letter.

gi gu.sanskrit: ī ring po la i'i zhes gi gu nyis brtsegs

senses.context: The constituent parts or factors making up spiritual practice (nyams len), rendered by Hopkins as "elements of practice." Here cha has the sense of a portion or component of the whole.
Tibetan transliteration of the Sanskrit proper name Guṇamati; identified by Hopkins as the name of a bodhisattva.

Given as an equivalent of the verb sgrig pa (past/imperative forms bsgrigs, sgrigs), in the sense of arranging or setting things in order. The comparanda supply only this verbal sense and do not clarify the force of the element gung here.

Personal name of a Tibetan scholar, dated 1762-1823, also known as Gung-thang Jam-pal-yang (gung thang 'jam dpal dbyangs). Gung thang here functions as the designation attached to the name; the remainder, dkon mchog bstan pa'i sgron me, is his personal name.
Alternative name of the Tibetan author otherwise called Gung-thang Kön-chog-ten-pay-drön-may (gung thang dkon mchog bstan pa'i sgron me), dated 1762-1823.
Modern term designating a communist. The comparanda give only this single English gloss.
Adverbial form of gud with the terminative du, indicating that something is set apart, kept separate, or done separately. Correlated with the Sanskrit prefix apa- in the sense of 'away, off, apart'.

gud du 'gro bar 'gyur cig.gloss: may he depart!; let him go away

senses.gloss: may he depart!; let him go away
senses.context: Optative/imperative phrase rendering Sanskrit apakrāmatu, expressing the wish or command that someone withdraw or take his leave. Built on gud du 'gro ba "to go apart, go aside, depart," with the imperative particle cig.

Corresponds to Sanskrit apakrāmati, the act of withdrawing from a place or company. The construction gud du song bar gyur uses the past stem of 'gro ba (song) with 'gyur, as against the optative form gud du 'gro bar 'gyur cig "may he depart."

gupta'i skabs.gloss: Gupta style; in the Gupta manner

senses.gloss: Gupta style; in the Gupta manner
senses.context: Glossed as "Gupta-style," i.e., pertaining to the Gupta period of India, used of such things as script or artistic form. The element skabs here marks the period or manner in question.

gur kum mdangs ldan.gloss: saffron-colored, having the hue of saffron

senses.gloss: saffron-colored, having the hue of saffron
senses.context: Descriptive compound: gur kum (saffron, crocus) plus mdangs ldan "possessing a hue/lustre," hence "saffron colored."
Literally "tent-home" (gur "tent, canopy" + khyim "house, home"), glossed as an abode or a mansion set up under a tent.
An intensified form of gus pa ("respect, reverence, devotion") qualified by chen po, "great." Used of an attitude of profound reverence or devotion directed toward an object worthy of honor.
A phyag (homage, salutation, prostration) performed with gus pa, respect or devotion. The compound stresses that the act of paying homage is made in an attitude of reverence.

gus par bya ba yid la byed pa.gloss: taking to mind an object to be respected; respectful mental engagement

senses.gloss: taking to mind an object to be respected; respectful mental engagement
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit satkṛtya-manaskāra, a mode of yid la byed pa (mental engagement, taking to mind) in which the object attended to is one that is to be honored, gus par bya ba. Listed among types of manaskāra in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials.
The negation of gus par byed pa, "to respect, to show reverence," corresponding to Sanskrit anādara. It denotes failing to treat something or someone with due honor.

senses.gloss: be indifferent; neglect; not be intent upon
senses.context: By extension the term covers inattentiveness or want of application, i.e., not applying oneself earnestly to something. Hopkins glosses it as "be indifferent; neglect; not be intent upon."

see_also: gus par bya ba yid la byed pa

senses.context: Past-tense form of gus par byed pa, corresponding to Sanskrit satkṛtya and sādara, i.e., acting with respect or reverence. The Chinese-Sanskrit gloss tradition explains satkṛtya by acts of formal honoring such as bestowing an insignia or preparing a maṇḍala, i.e., placing someone in a position of distinction.
Also given for kṛtātithya, "having offered the hospitality due to a guest." Here the respect shown takes the concrete form of receiving and entertaining a visitor.

see_also: gus par bya ba yid la byed pa

senses.context: A compound of gus (respect, reverence, earnestness) with sbyor (application, engagement), rendered by Hopkins as "intense application." It denotes applying oneself to practice with earnest respect rather than casually.

gegs su gyur pa.gloss: that which has become a hindrance

senses.gloss: that which has become a hindrance
senses.context: Literally "become an obstacle" (gegs su gyur pa), corresponding to Sanskrit vibandha/vibandhana and vighna. It designates whatever functions as an impediment, interference, or prevention with respect to a practice or attainment.

Also equated with vyavadhānabhūta, i.e., something that has come to stand in between and thus blocks or screens off. In this use it emphasizes the obstructing thing itself rather than the act of obstructing.

Negated form of go skabs 'byed pa, "to open an opening/opportunity," corresponding to Sanskrit (na) avakāśaṃ dadati. Conze's renderings have the sense "they are given no opportunity," i.e., no chance or opening is afforded.

go skabs ma mchis pa.gloss: there being no opportunity; no room

senses.gloss: there being no opportunity; no room
senses.context: Honorific-negative form corresponding to Sanskrit anavakāśa. It indicates the absence of any opening, chance, or room for something to occur.
By extension the term expresses impossibility: since no scope whatever is left, the thing in question cannot happen (Conze: "it cannot be").

Continuative form (go gyon te) of go gyon pa, corresponding to Sanskrit saṃnahati / saṃnahante, "puts on (the) armor." It typically introduces a following action, i.e., having put on the armor, one then does such-and-such.

Verbal phrase corresponding to Sanskrit sannaddha, said of one who has donned armor. In the comparanda the noun go cha renders 'armor' and bgos is the past of putting on/donning, the continuative shing linking it to a following clause.

go cha chen po bgos so.gloss: put on great armor; armed with the great armor

senses.gloss: put on great armor; armed with the great armor
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit mahā-sannāha-sannaddha, 'armed with the great armor.' The phrase states that one has donned the great armor (go cha chen po), the intensified form of the armor imagery reflected in go cha bgos.

go cha'i sgrub pa.gloss: achievement of armor; achieving through armor

senses.gloss: achievement of armor; achieving through armor
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit saṃnāha-pratipatti, in which saṃnāha is 'armor' and pratipatti is glossed as achieving or achievement. Hopkins allows the genitive to be read either as achieving by means of armor or as the achievement that is armor.
Transliterated proper name identified in the comparanda as Go-tan Khan, a Mongolian emperor. Attested only as a personal name, with no lexical meaning given.

go bde bar brjod.gloss: express in an easily understood form

senses.gloss: express in an easily understood form
senses.context: Verbal phrase in which brjod is 'express, state' and go bde bar is the adverbial 'so as to be easy to understand.' It describes stating something in a manner readily comprehended, the element go carrying the sense of understanding.
Adverbial phrase used when a series of items is to be matched one-by-one with a preceding or following series, i.e. 'in that same order'. Literally 'in accordance with the order (go rims)'.
Said of what is able to take up or fill a place or space (go sa). The comparandum indicates an ability to occupy, press upon, or cover a given area.
A place-name; the English gloss is marked as a provisional/tentative identification with Wakhan in Afghanistan. Formed with yul ('country, region') on gog.
Causal clause rendering Sanskrit ūrdhvaṃ gamana-yogāt, 'from being endowed with going upward'. It gives as a reason the fact of having movement or advancement in an upward direction.
Refers back to something that has been expressed or explained earlier in the text (gong du, 'above'), with brjod zin indicating that the statement is already completed.

see_also: gong du bshad ma thag pa

senses.context: Renders Sanskrit piṇḍa (with sapiṇḍa), the basic sense of a rounded lump or compacted mass of material. Hopkins glosses it simply as "lump; mass."
Also equated with mūrti and mūrtimat, i.e. a concrete form or that which possesses form. This extends the notion of a compacted mass to a shaped, embodied figure.
The equivalents piṭaka and samajyā suggest a gathered collection or assemblage. Here the term denotes things massed or brought together into one body.

gong ma gong ma'i lta ba go byed kyi ste.gloss: platform for causing understanding of the views of the higher schools

senses.gloss: platform for causing understanding of the views of the higher schools
senses.context: A descriptive phrase in which gong ma gong ma refers to the successively higher (tenet) systems, lta ba to their views, and stegs to a platform or stepping-place. Hopkins glosses it as a "platform for causing understanding of views of the higher [schools]," i.e. a basis serving as a step toward comprehending superior positions.

gong ma bas ches gong ma.gloss: much higher than the high; supreme among the higher

senses.gloss: much higher than the high; supreme among the higher
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit uttareṣv uttama / uttareṣūttamaḥ, "highest among the higher ones." The construction gong ma bas ches gong ma marks a degree of superiority exceeding even what is already superior.
Attested for Sanskrit uttarāsu bhūmiṣu, "on the higher grounds/levels." Hopkins renders it "high ground," with sa corresponding to bhūmi.
A compound of gong ma in the sense of sovereign or emperor with skyed tshal, a pleasure-grove or garden. Hopkins gives the phrasal rendering "imperial garden."

Formed from gong ma ("upper, higher, preceding") and spyi ("universal, general"), rendered by Hopkins as "vertical-universal." The comparanda support only this technical designation of a universal considered along an ascending or hierarchical (vertical) dimension, as opposed to one extending horizontally.

Rendered "grouse" by Hopkins and equated with a cluster of Sanskrit names for partridge-like birds: kapiñjala, tittiri, krakara, kakkubha, stambakari. The Sanskrit comparanda point to a francolin/partridge type of game bird.
Lokesh Chandra also records madhyāṃguli, "middle finger," for this term. This anatomical sense stands apart from the ornithological one and is attested here only by that single equivalent.

Equated with Sanskrit saṃlīyate, glossed by Hopkins as "becomes stolid," "despond," "is cowed." The term denotes a shrinking back or collapsing of spirit—losing heart or becoming dull and unresponsive.
Hopkins gives the honorific rendering "His Holiness," i.e., an elevated title of address built on gong ("above, upper"). The comparanda support only this honorific usage for a person of highest rank.
Lokesh Chandra records the Sanskrit equivalent udyukta, "applied, endeavoring, diligent." This sense is attested here solely by that equivalent and is unrelated to the honorific usage.

A phrase combining gong ("above, earlier in the text") with gsal ("clear, made clear") and the comparative particle ltar, glossed by Hopkins as "as clarified above [in the text]." It refers back to an explanation already given in a preceding portion of the same work.

see_also: gong du bshad ma thag pa

gom snyoms pa.gloss: walking at an even pace; evenness of stride

senses.gloss: walking at an even pace; evenness of stride
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit samakramatva, the quality of taking steps that are uniform and regular. Glossed by Hopkins as 'walks at an even pace', it describes a manner of gait rather than an act of measuring distance.

Corresponds to Sanskrit sakṛta-pāda-kṣepeṇa, literally 'by one casting/placing of the foot'. The Tibetan is instrumental (bor bas), indicating the means: something accomplished by taking just one step.

Hopkins glosses this as conditioning, familiarization, or accustoming, i.e. the process of becoming habituated to something through repetition. It belongs with the family of terms built on goms (habituation).

Corresponds to Sanskrit abhyāsavat, 'possessing practice/repetition', hence one who or that which is habituated. Hopkins renders it 'familiar; conditioned', and in one usage 'trained perceptions' (i.e. perceptions shaped by prior conditioning).
Also equated with Sanskrit kṛtin, 'one who has done (the work)', i.e. a skilled or practiced person. This sense highlights the possessor-noun value of the Tibetan -can suffix.

goms pa'i lam.gloss: path of familiarization; path of meditation

senses.gloss: path of familiarization; path of meditation
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit abhyāsa-mārga, the stage of the path consisting in repeated cultivation of what has already been seen or understood. Hopkins gives 'path of familiarization; path of conditioning', and in Conze's usage 'path of repeated meditational practice'.

A good quality (yon tan) that is to be developed through repeated practice or familiarization (goms pa), rendering Sanskrit abhyāsa-guṇa in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials. The compound marks such a quality as an object of cultivation rather than as already-present.
Phonetic Tibetan transcription of the Indic proper name Kauśambi. Attested only as a name-form in the comparanda, without further definition.
Glossed as 'circle', hence a rounded or circular form; the reduplicated form suggests a descriptive term for roundness. Compare the extended form gor gor po.

A garment (gos) that is distinguished or superior (khyad par du 'phags pa), corresponding to Sanskrit vastra-viśeṣaṇa in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra materials. Used of clothing singled out as fine or distinctive.
The patterns or figures (ri mo) worked into fine silk brocade (gos chen). Attested in the comparanda only as a descriptive phrase for such ornamented cloth.

Rendering nirupalepa / nirlepa / anupalipta, said of what bears no stain or defilement. Hopkins' glosses "without a stain, stainless, untainted, free from stains" indicate a quality of purity, i.e. nothing adheres to or soils it.
Literally "not being covered" (the negation of gos pa, to be covered/smeared). With niḥsaṅga the sense shades into being free of adherence or clinging.
The abstract form nirupalepatā shows the term can also name the quality itself, stainlessness or freedom from pollution.

gos la sogs pa ... tshol ba.gloss: to seek clothing and so forth

senses.gloss: to seek clothing and so forth
senses.context: Corresponds to cīvarādy-anveṣaṇa, the searching out of robes/garments and the other requisites. The phrase names such seeking as an activity, gos (clothing, robe) standing first in a list continued by la sogs pa.
Hopkins glosses this as "dishonesty", i.e. the quality of being devious or crooked in conduct. It is the positive counterpart of gya gyu med pa, "not crooked".
Translates akuṭila, negating the crookedness or deviousness expressed by gya gyu (ba). It thus characterizes what is straight or without dishonesty.
Corresponds to sudṛśa, and in the attested phrase sudṛśā devā, a named class of gods. The Tibetan renders the name descriptively, "sublime/auspicious appearance".
Taken literally, gya nom (excellent, sublime, auspicious) plus snang (appearance), i.e. fine or beautiful to behold.
A set title for a collection of eighteen works, identified in the comparanda as a Sa-kya collection. The name characterizes the eighteen texts as being of great renown (grags chen).
Rendering Sanskrit mahāyaśas/mahāyaśu, literally 'possessing (ldan) great renown (grags chen)'. Used as an epithet of one who is greatly famous.
Corresponds to Sanskrit mahāyaśas and yaśottara, i.e. fame that is highest or unsurpassed. It may function as a descriptive term for renown itself or as an epithet of one possessing such renown.
A sign or mark (rtags) that is correct or genuine (yang dag) and pertains to renown (grags). The comparanda supply only this literal rendering.
Contracted form equivalent to grags pa thob pa, 'one who has attained renown'. Used of a person who has obtained fame.
Rendering of Sanskrit viśālakīrti, given in the comparanda as the name of a tathāgata. The elements correspond literally to 'renown' (grags pa) that is 'vast, extensive' (rgya chen).
Corresponds to kīrtimat and yaśasvin, 'possessing fame'; the suffix can indicates possession of grags pa, renown. Also given for khyāta, 'well-known, celebrated'.
The comparanda also list nādita and ayaghuṣṭa, terms of sounding or proclaiming, reflecting the sense of grags as 'sound, being heard' as well as 'fame'.
Equated in the comparanda with the shorter form grags thob; the verb thob pa, 'to attain', indicates renown that has been acquired.
Formed with tsam, 'mere, only', qualifying grags pa, 'renown'; glossed simply as 'merely renowned', i.e. having only reputation and nothing further.
Corresponds to yaśo-hetutva, the state of being a cause (rgyu nyid) of fame or renown (yaśas, grags pa).

grags pa'i rtags.gloss: sign of renown; mark of being well known

senses.gloss: sign of renown; mark of being well known
senses.context: A compound of grags pa (renown, fame, being well known) and rtags (sign, mark), corresponding to a reconstructed *prasiddha-liṅga. It designates the indicator or token by which something is recognized as renowned or commonly acknowledged.
Formed from grang (number, count) with nges (definite, ascertained), glossed as a precise or definite enumeration. Used where a fixed count of items, rather than an open-ended list, is intended.

grang ba dang tsha ba la sogs pa'i sdug.gloss: sufferings of cold, heat, and so forth

senses.gloss: sufferings of cold, heat, and so forth
senses.context: Rendering śītaloṣṇādi ... duḥkha, this phrase names the physical sufferings brought on by cold, heat, and similar conditions. It occurs as a stock illustration of the ordinary bodily hardships of embodied existence.
Literally the sickness (nad) of cold (grang ba), corresponding to pratiśīta and glossed as rheumatism. A medical designation for an ailment attributed to cold.

see_also: grang ba dang tsha ba la sogs pa'i sdug bsngal

senses.context: A being who dwells in a cold hell, i.e. an inhabitant of the hells characterized by freezing torment, as distinct from the hot hells. Formed from grang (cold) and dmyal ba (hell).
Corresponds to Sanskrit gaṇanā, the act or process of counting or reckoning. Used for the tallying or enumeration of items.
Also given as an equivalent of Sanskrit śīta, 'cold'. In this sense the term belongs not to enumeration but to temperature/sensation.
A named meditative stabilization (ting nge 'dzin) characterized by counting or enumeration. The comparanda supply only the name, not its defining procedure.
Renders Sanskrit asaṃkhyeya, literally 'not to be counted'. Applied to quantities, durations, or qualities so vast as to be beyond reckoning; hence also rendered immeasurable, inestimable, infinite.
Renders Sanskrit dvyasaṃkhyeya-samāpti, the finishing or fulfilling of two periods of countless (asaṃkhyeya) eons. Used of the accomplishment of two of the incalculable periods of the path.
Renders Sanskrit saṃkhyātīta, 'gone beyond number'. Said of what exceeds any possible enumeration.

grangs su bgrang bar gtogs pa.gloss: included in the count, falling within enumeration

senses.gloss: included in the count, falling within enumeration
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit saṃkhyāṃ-gaṇanāṃ praviṣṭa, literally 'entered into number and counting', i.e. something that can be numbered or reckoned up. In the sources it commonly appears in negated form, whence Hopkins' rendering 'they have transcended all counting' (i.e. do not fall within enumeration).

grangs su 'gro.gloss: go in the count of, be reckoned among

senses.gloss: go in the count of, be reckoned among
senses.context: Translates saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / parisaṃkhyāta: to enter into the reckoning, to be counted or included in a given number or class.

senses.gloss: come to be styled or called, derive one's name from
senses.context: Idiomatically the same expression indicates that something acquires a designation or is spoken of under a certain name, e.g. 'is called', 'derives his name from', 'it gives sense to say'.

grangs su 'gro 'gyur ro.gloss: will be reckoned among, will go in the count of

senses.gloss: will be reckoned among, will go in the count of
senses.context: A finite verbal form of grangs su 'gro, corresponding to parisaṃkhyāta, 'reckoned up as'. It states that something is to be counted or included within a specified number or category.

grangs su mchi'o.gloss: goes in the count of, is reckoned as (honorific/elevated)

senses.gloss: goes in the count of, is reckoned as (honorific/elevated)
senses.context: An elevated verbal form corresponding to saṃkhyāṃ gacchati, equivalent in sense to grangs su 'gro: to enter the reckoning, be counted among. It also carries the idiomatic sense 'comes to be styled/called', 'derives its name from'.
Given for Sanskrit ujjaṅgala 'arid, dry waste land' and uccharkara 'gravelly, full of grit', hence a dry, stony or sandy stretch of ground.

gral rked.gloss: middle of the row; middle rank

senses.gloss: middle of the row; middle rank
senses.context: The middle portion of a seating row or ranked line, between the upper/front part (gral stod) and the lower end (gral 'og, gral gsham). Used of a person's place or standing within a graded assembly.

gral stod.gloss: upper part of the row; front rank

senses.gloss: upper part of the row; front rank
senses.context: The higher or forward section of a seating row, where those of superior standing are placed. Contrasts with the middle (gral rked) and lower end (gral 'og, gral gsham) of the same row.

gral mtho sa.gloss: head of the row; place of honor

senses.gloss: head of the row; place of honor
senses.context: The high or honored position at the head of a line or seating order in an assembly. Opposed to the lower positions of the row (gral 'og, gral gsham).

gral 'og.gloss: lower part of a row; end of a row

senses.gloss: lower part of a row; end of a row
senses.context: The lower or final portion of a seating row or ranked line, where those of lesser standing are placed. Contrasts with the upper part or head of the row (gral stod, gral mtho sa).

gral rim.gloss: row, line, series (Skt. paṅkti, rāji, śreṇī)

senses.gloss: row, line, series (Skt. paṅkti, rāji, śreṇī)
senses.context: A row or line of things arranged in order; rendered by Sanskrit paṅkti, rāji, and śreṇī. The emphasis is on serial arrangement, i.e. the sequence in which items or persons are lined up.

By extension, the graded order of places in an assembly, hence the ranking or precedence assigned within it. Positions within such an order are specified as upper, middle, or lower (gral stod, gral rked, gral 'og).

see_also: gral rims su ma bab par 'gril du 'jug pa la ma bzlog par za ba

senses.context: Rendered by Sanskrit catura and paṭu, both denoting quickness of mind and dexterity. Used of a person who is sharp, deft, and capable.
Hopkins gives the sense "taut," i.e. drawn tight or held firmly, as of something stretched or tightened. This physical sense stands beside the sense of mental sharpness.
Corresponds to Sanskrit āsāra, a downpour of rain; Hopkins glosses it as "fertile rain," i.e. rain that brings growth. The comparanda support only this meteorological sense.
Equated with Sanskrit nāva/nau (boat, ship), pota and vohittha (ship, vessel); the form nāvi occurs in the {C} materials. Hopkins likewise gives "boat; ship."
Hopkins glosses this as "rudder," the part that holds or steers a boat (gru); the Tibetan literally means "boat-holder."
Also used to render Sanskrit potala/potalaka (and the form modralya recorded by Lokesh Chandra), the name of a place. The comparanda give no further specification beyond the name.

gru 'dzin bdag po.gloss: Lord of the Potala, epithet of Avalokiteśvara

senses.gloss: Lord of the Potala, epithet of Avalokiteśvara
senses.context: Formed from gru 'dzin (Potala/Potalaka) with bdag po, "lord, master." Hopkins identifies the referent as Avalokiteśvara, who presides over that place.

Title of a versified root text setting forth Buddhist and non-Buddhist tenet systems (grub mtha'), composed by Jam-yang-shay-pa. It serves as the basis for his own commentary, known in short title as the Great Exposition of Tenets (grub mtha' chen mo).

see_also: grub mtha' kun shes nas mtha' bral sgrub pa zhes bya ba'i bstan bcos rnam par bshad pa legs bshad kyi rgya mtsho

grub mtha' bzhi'i lugs kyi kun rdzob dan.gloss: Explanation of the Conventional and the Ultimate in the Four Systems of Tenets: The Spring Cuckoo's Song of Good Explanations

senses.gloss: Explanation of the Conventional and the Ultimate in the Four Systems of Tenets: The Spring Cuckoo's Song of Good Explanations
senses.context: Title of a treatise by Ngag-wang-pal-dan (ngag dbang dpal ldan, b. 1797) explaining how the two truths — the conventional and the ultimate — are presented in each of the four Buddhist systems of tenets.

Title of a well-known presentation of tenets (grub mtha'i rnam bzhag) by Kön-chog-jig-may-wang-po (dkon mchog 'jigs med dbang po, 1728–91), setting out the assertions of the various philosophical systems.

grub mtha'i rnam bzhag.gloss: presentation of tenets; establishment of tenet systems

senses.gloss: presentation of tenets; establishment of tenet systems
senses.context: The systematic setting forth of the assertions of philosophical systems (grub mtha'), Sanskrit *siddhāntavyavasthāpana. The term also designates a genre of Tibetan literature devoted to expounding the positions of the several schools.

see_also: grub mtha' kun shes nas mtha' bral sgrub pa zhes bya ba'i bstan bcos rnam par bshad pa legs bshad kyi rgya mtsho

grub mthas bslad pa la ltos med du.gloss: without relying on being affected by tenets

senses.gloss: without relying on being affected by tenets
senses.context: Adverbial phrase indicating that something occurs or is posited without depending on the mind's having been influenced or conditioned by adherence to a philosophical system (grub mtha'). Used of awareness or conceptions that arise independently of doctrinal indoctrination.

grub pa dus mnyam/ gnas pa dus mnyam/ 'j.gloss: simultaneous in establishment, abiding, and disintegration

senses.gloss: simultaneous in establishment, abiding, and disintegration
senses.context: A set phrase applied to factors that are established (produced), abide, and disintegrate at the same time as one another. Hopkins renders the key element as "established simultaneously," i.e., simultaneously (dus mnyam).

Sanskrit siddhi-pūrvaṃgama-maṅgalatva (MSA): the state of being an auspicious sign that goes before, and thus heralds, an achievement. Hopkins glosses it as "auspiciousness preceding a feat/yogic achievement," i.e., grub pa (siddhi) here is a yogic attainment or accomplished feat.

grub pa'i mtha' spyi.gloss: general tenets; general presentation of tenets

senses.gloss: general tenets; general presentation of tenets
senses.context: Formed from grub pa'i mtha' (tenets, philosophical system) plus spyi (general), designating tenets treated in general rather than a particular system. Hopkins gives "general tenets" (a phrase reconstruction).
A deity associated with grub pa in the sense of attainment or magical accomplishment (siddhi). Hopkins offers the phrase rendering "god of magical accomplishment."

Sanskrit niṣpanna-bodha (MSA): the understanding or realization that something is completed or brought to accomplishment. Hopkins glosses it as "realize that it has been established/accomplished/achieved/completed," so grub par gyur pa is the state of having been fully achieved.
An excellent or foremost friend or companion; the Sanskrit saciva suggests an associate or attendant who accompanies and assists. Formed from grogs (friend, accompanier) with mchog (supreme, best).
In abstract usage, corresponding to sumitratā, the state of having good friends or the quality of supreme friendship.

grogs snying rje chen pos zin cing.gloss: affected by great compassion as its accompanier

senses.gloss: affected by great compassion as its accompanier
senses.context: A phrase describing something (e.g. a mind or practice) that is held or seized by great compassion functioning as its accompanying factor. Here grogs has the sense of accompanier or assisting companion rather than 'friend' in the social sense.
The strength or force supplied by a friend, companion, or assisting factor (Sanskrit mitra-bala). Used where the support of an accompanier is itself counted as a source of power.

A friend or close associate; the Sanskrit equivalents sahāya, suhṛt, and sahāyatā cover both the person who keeps company and the state of companionship. saṅgama further suggests association or coming together.
In extended usage, a factor or condition that accompanies and assists something else, rendering sahāya in the sense of helper or support.

grogs pa la dad che bar mi 'gyur.gloss: does not become greatly attached to a companion

senses.gloss: does not become greatly attached to a companion
senses.context: A phrase rendering the Sanskrit (na) saṃvāsa-śīlā bhavati, i.e. one is not given to habitually dwelling together with a companion. Conze's English suggests abstaining from habitual cohabitation, though the correspondence between the Tibetan (literally 'does not come to have great faith/attachment toward a companion') and the Sanskrit is uncertain.

grogs po 'dra ba.gloss: like a friend, comparable to a companion

senses.gloss: like a friend, comparable to a companion
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit mitra-kalpa, a comparison formed with -kalpa ("resembling, like") on mitra ("friend"). Used of someone or something that acts in the manner of a friend, companion, or helper without necessarily being one in the full sense.

Renders hīnaiḥ sahāyaiḥ parivāritaḥ, where sahāya means companion/helper, hīna "low, inferior," and parivārita "encircled, surrounded on all sides." Describes a person whose entire circle of associates is of low or base quality.
Renders mitrād āttā, i.e., something received or taken (ātta) from a friend (mitra, ablative). Refers to what one has obtained from a companion rather than acquired on one's own.

Renders kumitra, formed with the pejorative prefix ku- on mitra ("friend"); the Tibetan likewise adds ngan pa ("bad, evil") to grogs po. Denotes one who has the appearance of a friend but is harmful or unreliable, in contrast to an excellent companion.

grogs bya ba la skyo ba med pa.gloss: not discouraged in acting as a companion/helper

senses.gloss: not discouraged in acting as a companion/helper
senses.context: Renders sāhāyya-kriyā-akheda: the absence of weariness or discouragement (akheda) in performing the act (kriyā) of assistance or companionship (sāhāyya). Describes untiring willingness to accompany and help others.

see_also: grogs gi rim gro byas pas
grogs snying rje chen pos zin cing

grogs tshul khrims dang lta ba mthun pa.gloss: companionship with those of concordant ethics and view

senses.gloss: companionship with those of concordant ethics and view
senses.context: Renders sabhāga-śīla-dṛṣṭi-sahāyakatva: the state of having as one's friend or companion someone whose ethical discipline (śīla) and view (dṛṣṭi) are of the same class as one's own. Used of the quality of association with like-minded fellows in practice.

senses.gloss: friend/companion with concordant ethics and view
senses.context: In its concrete use the phrase designates the person himself — a companion who accords with one in discipline and in view.

Equivalent to susahāyaka and susakhā, a companion who is beneficial or excellent. The Sanskrit comparanda point to the sense of a well-suited helper or associate rather than a merely pleasant acquaintance.

grogs su gyur pa.gloss: friendship; state of being a companion

senses.gloss: friendship; state of being a companion
senses.context: Rendering sahāyatva, the abstract condition of serving as someone's friend, helper, or companion.

senses.gloss: became a friend, came to be a companion
senses.context: Corresponding to sahāyībhāvaṃ gataḥ, of one who has entered into the state of being another's companion or helper.
Rendering paurī, one belonging to or living in a city (grong khyer). Used of the inhabitants of a town as distinct from those of the countryside.

grong 'jug gi rnal 'byor.gloss: yoga of transference into another body

senses.gloss: yoga of transference into another body
senses.context: Renders parakāya-praveśa-yoga, the yogic practice of entering into another's body (glossed in English as entering a dead body). The Tibetan grong 'jug, literally 'entering the town/dwelling', is used for this transfer of consciousness into a corporeal support.

Variant spelling of gling phran brgyad, the eight subsidiary continents (gling phran) of traditional cosmology that accompany the four principal continents (gling bzhi). Hopkins glosses it as "eight minor continent(s)."

gling bzhi gling phran brgyad.gloss: the four major and eight minor temples

senses.gloss: the four major and eight minor temples
senses.context: A set enumeration combining gling bzhi and gling phran brgyad; Hopkins renders it as "four major and eight minor temples," i.e. gling here designates edifices rather than land-masses. The same compound underlies the cosmological grouping of four continents with their eight subcontinents.

gling bzhi gling phran bcu gnyis.gloss: the twelve major and minor continents

senses.gloss: the twelve major and minor continents
senses.context: The four continents (gling bzhi) together with their eight subcontinents (gling phran), counted as twelve in all. Hopkins glosses the compound as "twelve major and minor continents."
Descriptive term glossed by Hopkins as "four-sided; with four sides," applied to something of quadrangular shape. The formation is based on gling bzhi with the nominalizing/adjectival -ma.

gling bzhi'i mi.gloss: the humans of the four continents

senses.gloss: the humans of the four continents
senses.context: The human inhabitants of the four principal continents (gling bzhi) of traditional cosmology. Compare the parallel expression for the people of the eight minor continents, gling phran brgyad kyi mi.

Designation of the eight subsidiary land-masses that accompany the main continents in the traditional cosmology, i.e. two attendants for each of the four continents. The headword pairs two ways of naming them, gling g.yog ('attendant continents') and gling phran ('minor/lesser continents').
A class of nāga spirits characterized as mischievous or troublesome. Here glu stands for the nāga (serpent-spirit) class rather than 'song', as also in glu bsen mo, 'evil female nāga'.

A generation of the altruistic mind of enlightenment illustrated by the simile of melodious song. The term belongs to the series of similes used to classify types of bodhicitta generation, glu dbyangs, 'song, melody', supplying the comparison.
A malevolent female nāga; bsen mo indicates the harmful female demoness type. As in glu gyan, glu here designates the nāga class rather than 'song'.

glegs bam du chud par.gloss: contained in a book, put into written form

senses.gloss: contained in a book, put into written form
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit pustaka-gata, 'gone into a book': of teachings or words that have been included in, or committed to, a written volume.

senses.gloss: gotten from a book, mere book-learning
senses.context: In some contexts the same phrase describes knowledge acquired only from a text rather than from realization or direct instruction, hence 'has got it from a book, from a book'.

glegs bam du bris nas.gloss: having written (it) down in a book

senses.gloss: having written (it) down in a book
senses.context: Gerundive phrase corresponding to Sanskrit pustaka-likhitāṃ kṛtvā, i.e. having put a text into written form as a volume. Typically used of committing a teaching to writing in book form as a meritorious act.

Renders Sanskrit kapāṭa (board, door-panel), paṭṭa/paṭṭikā (plate, tablet, strip), tāmra-paṭṭa (copper plate) and suvarṇa-patra (gold leaf/plate). Thus a flat rigid piece serving as writing or inscription surface, or as a book-cover board.
By extension the individual leaf or page of a manuscript volume, and a written label or tag; Hopkins gives 'page; label'.

Translates Sanskrit nidāna, the opening narrative or statement of the occasion/setting of a discourse. Hopkins also records the extended use for 'specific teachings', i.e. teachings given with reference to a particular occasion.

see_also: gleng gzhi dang gang zag bsdus pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa

gleng gzhi'i sde.gloss: the introduction section (nidāna), the class of introductory scriptures

senses.gloss: the introduction section (nidāna), the class of introductory scriptures
senses.context: Renders Sanskrit nidāna with the added element sde, 'section, class', hence the introductory portion of a discourse or the corresponding scriptural category. Hopkins glosses 'introduction; specific teachings', the latter reflecting teachings tied to a particular occasion.

see_also: gleng gzhi dang gang zag bsdus pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa

senses.context: Past/perfect form of gleng (gleng, gleng, glengs, glengs) meaning to speak of, mention, express, propound; compare kathayiṣyāmi, 'I shall relate'.
In the Conze materials rendering vyāpārita, 'set to work, employed'.
Verbal form (past/nominalized) of gleng, glossed by Sanskrit abhihita, 'said, spoken, uttered.' Used of speaking, mentioning, or expressing something in discourse.

senses.gloss: brought up (as a topic), previously mentioned
senses.context: The equivalent pūrvādhikṛta points to a topic that has been introduced or taken up beforehand. In this use the term marks something already raised or set forth in the preceding discussion.

Personal name of a Tibetan author; the comparanda supply only the phonetic rendering of the name. The initial element glo appears to function as a place or lineage designation, followed by the title mkhan chen ('great abbot') and the personal name bsod nams lhun grub.

Renders Sanskrit āgantukamala, a defilement that is 'incoming' or extrinsic rather than intrinsic to what it stains. The element glo bur conveys the sudden or accidental, non-essential character of such a stain.

see_also: glo bur dri bral gyi cha
glo bur dri bral gyi myang 'das

senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit āgantukatva, the state of being adventitious or incidental. Said of what comes about accidentally or abruptly rather than as something intrinsic.

glo bur dri bral gyi cha.gloss: factor of freedom from adventitious defilements

senses.gloss: factor of freedom from adventitious defilements
senses.context: A compound of glo bur ('adventitious') with dri bral ('freed from stain/defilement') and cha ('factor, aspect'). It designates the aspect or factor consisting in being separated from defilements that are merely adventitious.

see_also: glo bur dri bral gyi myang 'das

senses.context: The aspect or portion (cha) of purity that is adventitious (glo bur), i.e. purity conceived as arising incidentally rather than as intrinsic. Formed in parallel with the phrase for the factor of separation from adventitious defilement.

see_also: glo bur dri bral gyi cha

senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit āgantukatva, the state of having arisen incidentally or unexpectedly rather than belonging to something intrinsically. Used of what occurs suddenly or comes as an adventitious visitor to what it affects.
A descriptive phrase glossed as 'lightning-like', characterizing something by its resemblance to the flash of lightning. The comparanda support only this general simile-based reading.
Corresponds to Sanskrit vidyut, the flash or streak of lightning. Frequently the basis of similes for what is momentary or instantaneous.
Verbal-nominal variant of glog 'gyu, glossed as a flash of lightning. Same referent as the shorter form, which is equated with Sanskrit vidyut.

A named samādhi rendering Sanskrit vidyutopama, 'like lightning', i.e. a meditative stabilization characterized by the simile of a lightning flash. It belongs to the series of similarly named concentrations designated by an image.

see_also: glog gi sgron ma zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin
glog gi 'od ces bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin

senses.context: Verb of slackening or easing tension, whether of something physically taut or of mental effort; Hopkins gives 'loosen, relax'.
Extended sense of letting go or freeing, corresponding to Hopkins 'release; set free'; the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra equivalent given is samavaghāta.

glod pa.sanskrit: glod pa/ glod pa/ glod pa/ glod pa/; {MSA}samavaghāta

senses.context: Paired designation for the twofold division of phenomena into negative phenomena (dgag pa) and positive phenomena (sgrub pa).
In the context of debate and reasoning, the pair consisting of refuting an opponent's position and establishing or proving one's own.

see_also: dgag pa dngos su rtogs pa'i tshad ma

dgag sgrub byed.gloss: refutation and establishment; refutation and proof

senses.gloss: refutation and establishment; refutation and proof
senses.context: The paired activities of negating an opponent's thesis and proving one's own, treated as a single compound term in reasoning and debate.

see_also: dgag pa dngos su rtogs pa'i tshad ma

dgag pa dngos su rtogs pa'i tshad ma.gloss: direct perception explicitly realizing a negative phenomenon

senses.gloss: direct perception explicitly realizing a negative phenomenon
senses.context: A valid cognizer (tshad ma) that realizes a negative phenomenon (dgag pa) explicitly (dngos su) rather than merely implicitly. Hopkins glosses it as a direct perception so realizing a negative phenomenon.

see_also: dgag pa'i rnam pa shar nas dgag pa la gsar du mi bslu ba'i rig pa
dgag par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa

senses.context: A word or verbal expression that states a negation, i.e., a term whose function is to negate (dgag pa) rather than to affirm. Contrasted implicitly with terms of affirmation (sgrub pa) in the negative/positive (dgag sgrub) pairing.

dgag pa'i rnam pa shar nas dgag pa la gs.gloss: knower newly incontrovertible regarding a negative phenomenon, with the aspect of that negative appearing

senses.gloss: knower newly incontrovertible regarding a negative phenomenon, with the aspect of that negative appearing
senses.context: A technical definition-style term for a consciousness (rig pa) that is newly (gsar du) non-deceptive (mi bslu ba) with respect to a negative phenomenon (dgag pa), where the aspect (rnam pa) of that negative dawns to it. As the comparanda indicate, this specifies a valid cognizer characterized both by the appearance of the negative aspect and by fresh incontrovertibility.

see_also: dgag pa dngos su rtogs pa'i tshad ma

dgag par gyur pa'i ldog pa rigs gcig pa.gloss: negative phenomena that are the same isolate type

senses.gloss: negative phenomena that are the same isolate type
senses.context: Phenomena that are negatives (dgag pa) and that belong to one and the same type of isolate (ldog pa rigs gcig pa). The expression classifies negatives by sameness of isolate-type.

dgag bya bkag pa'i med 'gag.gloss: non-affirming negation that is the mere negation of the object of negation

senses.gloss: non-affirming negation that is the mere negation of the object of negation
senses.context: A negation consisting simply in the elimination (bkag pa) of the object to be negated (dgag bya), leaving nothing posited in its place — hence a non-affirming negative (med dgag / med 'gag). The Hopkins gloss is marked as a provisional rendering.

dgag bya khyab ches pa.gloss: too extensive an object of negation

senses.gloss: too extensive an object of negation
senses.context: An object of negation or refutation (dgag bya) identified too broadly, its scope (khyab) being excessive. The term flags a fault in delimiting what is to be negated.

dgag bya 'gog pa'i rtog pa.gloss: conceptual consciousness that [merely] refutes an object of negation

senses.gloss: conceptual consciousness that [merely] refutes an object of negation
senses.context: A thought-consciousness whose activity consists only in eliminating (dgag pa) the dgag bya, the object to be negated. As Hopkins' gloss stresses with 'merely', such a conceptual awareness accomplishes negation alone and is not credited with establishing anything positive.

see_also: dgag pa'i rnam pa shar nas dgag pa la gsar du mi bslu ba'i rig pa

senses.context: Rendered by the Sanskrit spṛhati / spṛhanti in Lokesh Chandra, i.e. to yearn for or take delight in something, consistent with the root dga' 'joy, gladness'.
Hopkins records this rendering from Conze's Prajñāpāramitā vocabulary ({C}); no further context for the usage is supplied by the comparanda.
A doubled expression of gladness (dga' + mgu), glossed by Hopkins as 'immense joy' and by Lokesh Chandra with praharṣa, intense delight or elation.
The alternative Sanskrit equivalent susthita suggests the sense of being in a settled, thoroughly happy state; the comparanda give no further specification.
Corresponds to Sanskrit rati-yukta (MSA), 'joined with delight'; used of a person or state that is accompanied by joy or happiness.

dga' ldan 'khri pa.gloss: holder of the Gan-den throne; head of the Ge-luk-pa order

senses.gloss: holder of the Gan-den throne; head of the Ge-luk-pa order
senses.context: Title of the incumbent of the abbatial throne ('khri) of Gan-den (dga' ldan) monastery, who according to Hopkins functions as head of the Ge-luk-pa order.

Verbal phrase for the direct, felt experiencing of joy or pleasure, corresponding to Sanskrit sukham anubhavati. The emphasis falls on undergoing or savoring the pleasant state oneself (nyams su myong ba), not merely on possessing it.
Phrase for the acquisition or gaining of joy (prīti), rendering Sanskrit prīti-lābha as well as simple prīti. Used where delight or happiness is something newly won or come by.

Renders Sanskrit prīti-sukha-saṃjananī / prītisukhajananī, i.e., that which produces or engenders the pair joy (dga' ba = prīti) and bliss (bde ba = sukha). May be used verbally (to produce joy and bliss) or attributively of what causes them.

Renders Sanskrit prīti-sukha-saṃvedana, the full or complete experiencing (yang dag par myong ba) of the pair joy (prīti) and bliss (sukha). The prefix yang dag par corresponds to the intensifying saṃ-, indicating experience that is complete or genuine.
Attributive phrase for one who possesses joy or delight, glossed by Sanskrit ramamāṇa (delighting, taking pleasure) and saktāhlāda. Equivalent in form to dga' dang ldan pa.

In some Prajñāpāramitā-related material the phrase is recorded as equivalent to Sanskrit hrīmat, rendered 'modest' (i.e., possessing a sense of shame or decorum); this sense is attested only in that comparandum.

dga' ba ni bde ba dang mi 'bral ba'i rna.gloss: joy has the aspect of non-separation from happiness

senses.gloss: joy has the aspect of non-separation from happiness
senses.context: A definitional formula (Skt. muditā sukhāviyogākārā) explaining the immeasurable/attitude of joy: its aspect or mode of apprehension is [the wish for] beings' non-separation from happiness or pleasure. Here dga' ba renders muditā, joy, and the phrase specifies what distinguishes it by way of its aspect (rnam pa, ākāra).
Renders Skt. rati-jaha, one who has given up or left behind delight (rati). Used of forsaking joy or pleasurable attachment.
Renders Skt. rati-kara, that which makes or produces delight; hence 'giving joy'.
Corresponding to Skt. muditāyata, in the sense of engaging in or being devoted to joy (muditā) as a cultivated attitude.

dga' ba yid la byed pa.gloss: mental contemplation of joy, taking joy to mind

senses.gloss: mental contemplation of joy, taking joy to mind
senses.context: Renders a family of Sanskrit compounds in -manaskāra/-manasikāra (mental attention or contemplation) with terms for joy, gladness, delight, or eager wish (pramoda, prīyaṇā, rati, spṛhā). Thus: bringing joy to mind, or a joyous act of mental attention.
Renders Skt. ruci-paripāka: the complete ripening or maturing of joy (ruci, delight, liking). Describes joy brought to full development.

Rendered from Sanskrit tuṣṭi-viśeṣotpādana, the term denotes the producing or generating (bskyed pa, utpādana) of a distinctive or special (khyad par, viśeṣa) satisfaction or joy (dga' ba, tuṣṭi). Hopkins glosses it as generating a particular, specific type or instance of joy.
From Sanskrit rati-hetutva, the abstract term for the state of being a cause (rgyu nyid, hetutva) of joy or delight (dga' ba, rati). Hopkins gives simply 'cause of joy'.

dga' ba'i rang bzhin can bde ba'i rang b.gloss: having a pleasing and pleasant nature

senses.gloss: having a pleasing and pleasant nature
senses.context: A paired expression rendering Sanskrit priya-rūpa-sāta-rūpa, i.e., that which has the nature (rang bzhin can, -rūpa) of being dear or pleasing (dga' ba, priya) together with the nature of being agreeable or comfortable (bde ba, sāta). Conze's translation is 'dear and pleasant forms', with Hopkins noting that 'things' would render the second member better than 'forms'.
From Sanskrit prīti-rasa (also ratirasa), the flavor or savor (ro, rasa) of joy or delight (dga' ba, prīti/rati). Hopkins glosses it as 'taste of joy'.
Rendering Sanskrit muditāśaya, a compound of muditā (joy, gladness) and āśaya (thought, attitude, intention; bsam pa). Hopkins glosses it as 'joyous thought' or 'thought of joy'.

Divinatory figure of the sort used in Tibetan astrological calculation; the comparanda give only the equivalence with 'trigram'. Formed with dgung (sky, celestial sphere), suggesting a celestial/calendrical context of use.
A break or period of rest from regular work or study, e.g. a monastic or school recess. Second element seng conveys the sense of a gap or interval within the ongoing round of days.

dgun sgang.gloss: the winter period, depth of winter

senses.gloss: the winter period, depth of winter
senses.context: Designates winter considered as a stretch of the year, glossed as 'period of winter'. Formed from dgun (winter) with sgang, indicating the full or high part of the season.

dgun chung.gloss: late winter, the last part of winter

senses.gloss: late winter, the last part of winter
senses.context: Names the closing portion of the winter season, glossed 'late-winter [season]'. Contrasts with terms for the main body or height of winter.
One who instructs students, whether in a monastic or secular educational setting. Built on dge (virtue, the wholesome) with rgan (elder, senior), i.e. a senior figure in matters of virtuous training.

Name of a class of deities, rendered in the comparanda by Sanskrit śubhakṛtsṇā (devā), i.e. gods whose virtue or splendor is 'entirely/wholly good'. The comparanda identify only the divine class-name; no further doctrinal detail is supported.

dge bcu'i las kyi lam.gloss: path of the ten virtuous actions

senses.gloss: path of the ten virtuous actions
senses.context: Corresponds to Sanskrit daśa-kuśala-karma-patha, the set of ten courses of wholesome action. The term names these ten as a 'path' (las kyi lam, karma-patha) of virtue.
Contraction of dge ba'i chos, corresponding to Sanskrit kuśala-dharma. Used of doctrines or qualities/factors that are virtuous or wholesome.

dge bsnyen dang dge bsnyen ma gnyis.gloss: the two: laymen and laywomen with vows (upāsaka and upāsikā)

senses.gloss: the two: laymen and laywomen with vows (upāsaka and upāsikā)
senses.context: An enumerative pairing of the male lay vow-holder (dge bsnyen, upāsaka) with the female lay vow-holder (dge bsnyen ma, upāsikā). The comparanda present it simply as a pair counted together as 'the two'.

Corresponds to Sanskrit śubhāśubhādhi(-), i.e. the producing or bringing about of what is virtuous (śubha) and what is non-virtuous (aśubha). The comparanda support only this general sense of generating both kinds of action.

dge bdun dkon mchog rjes su dran pa.gloss: recollection of the Jewel of the Spiritual Community (Saṅgha)

senses.gloss: recollection of the Jewel of the Spiritual Community (Saṅgha)
senses.context: One of the recollections directed at the Three Jewels, here calling to mind the qualities of the spiritual community as an object of religious remembrance. The headword combines 'dge 'dun' (spiritual community) with 'dkon mchog' (jewel) and 'rjes su dran pa' (recollection, mindfulness).

dge 'dun rgya mtsho.gloss: Gendün Gyatso (1476-1542), the Second Dalai Lama

senses.gloss: Gendün Gyatso (1476-1542), the Second Dalai Lama
senses.context: Proper name of the Tibetan hierarch identified as the second Dalai Lama, whose dates are given as 1476-1542.
Skt. saṃghānusmṛti: the practice of calling to mind the spiritual community, one of the standard set of recollections. Rendered both as 'mindfulness' and as 'recollection' of the Saṅgha.

dge 'dun nyi shu'i mdo.gloss: sūtra passages on the twenty members of the spiritual community

senses.gloss: sūtra passages on the twenty members of the spiritual community
senses.context: Refers to scriptural passages setting out the twenty divisions or members (nyi shu) of the āryan spiritual community (dge 'dun).
Skt. mahāsāṃghika: name of an early Buddhist school, literally the school of the 'great (phal chen) assembly/community (dge 'dun)'.

dge 'dun zhal grangs.gloss: census of the saṅgha, head-count of monks

senses.gloss: census of the saṅgha, head-count of monks
senses.context: A tally of the number of members of a monastic community. The comparanda gloss the term only as a census or head-count of the saṅgha, i.e. a reckoning of how many monastics there are.

dge ba goms pa.gloss: cultivating virtue; becoming habituated to virtue

senses.gloss: cultivating virtue; becoming habituated to virtue
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit śubhābhyāsa, the repeated practice or habituation (goms pa) of what is virtuous or good (dge ba, śubha). The comparanda support both the sense of actively cultivating virtue and that of becoming accustomed to it through repetition.

dge ba sgom pa.gloss: meditating on virtue; meditative cultivation of virtue

senses.gloss: meditating on virtue; meditative cultivation of virtue
senses.context: Rendering Sanskrit śubha-bhāvanā, the meditation on or meditative cultivation (sgom pa, bhāvanā) of virtue (dge ba, śubha). The comparanda indicate that virtue is here the object or content of meditative development.

Rendering Sanskrit śubha-nirhāra, the bringing forth, accomplishment, or achievement (sgrub pa, nirhāra) of what is virtuous (dge ba, śubha). The comparanda present it as the actual realization of virtue rather than mere aspiration to it.

Rendering Sanskrit kuśalābhinirhāra-nimitta, an aspect or characteristic mark (rnam pa, nimitta) of the accomplishment (abhinirhāra) of virtue (dge ba, kuśala). The comparanda support only the general gloss 'aspect of achieving virtue' and specify nothing further about what such aspects are.

The intention or attitude (āśaya) directed toward virtuous conduct (śubha-vṛtti), i.e. the aspiration to take up and practice what is wholesome. Attested in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra contexts describing the practitioner's motivation with respect to virtuous behavior.
A pair of virtues or wholesome factors (śubha-dvaya) enumerated as a set. The comparanda give only the numerical designation, without specifying the members of the pair.

The cultivation or bringing into being (bhāvanā) of what is wholesome (kuśala), i.e. developing virtues through meditative practice. Used in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra passages listing what a practitioner is to cultivate.
Rendering śubhin, said of a person or state that possesses virtue or the wholesome. Used adjectivally to characterize one who is furnished with virtue.

dge ba dang mi dge ba'i las kyi lam dang.gloss: knowledge of the varieties of virtuous and non-virtuous paths of action and their effects

senses.gloss: knowledge of the varieties of virtuous and non-virtuous paths of action and their effects
senses.context: An exhaustive knowledge (jñāna) of the diversity (vaicitrya) of wholesome and unwholesome paths of action (kuśala-akuśala-karma-patha) together with their respective fruits (phala). Listed in Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra contexts among forms of knowledge concerning karma and its results.

dge ba 'dod pa.gloss: desiring virtue; wishing for the virtuous

senses.gloss: desiring virtue; wishing for the virtuous
senses.context: Rendering Skt. kuśala-ruci, an inclination or taste for what is virtuous (kuśala). Used of one whose wish or aspiration is directed toward virtuous states and deeds.
Also given for Skt. kuśalavāda, where 'dod pa carries the sense of asserting or professing what is virtuous rather than merely desiring it.
Rendering Skt. ameya-śubhatāśraya, the support (āśraya, gnas) of unmeasurable goodness (śubhatā). Names that which serves as the ground from which immeasurable virtue arises.
Rendering Skt. kuśala-vivardhana and śubha-vṛddhi, the augmentation or flourishing of virtue (kuśala, śubha). Applies both to the process of virtue increasing and to that which causes it to increase.

dge ba bya ba.gloss: doing what is virtuous; acting well

senses.gloss: doing what is virtuous; acting well
senses.context: Literally 'performing virtue'; given for Skt. kalyāṇa, that which is good, wholesome, or beneficial. Glossed also as helpful, good, lovely.
Rendering Skt. śubhānuttaryāvaraṇa, an obscuration (āvaraṇa, sgrib pa) that blocks the highest, unsurpassable (anuttarya) goodness (śubha). Named as one of the obstructions to be removed on the path.
Negated form of dge ba (virtue), rendering Sanskrit akuśala. Used of actions, mental states, or phenomena that are unwholesome, i.e., not virtuous.

Corresponds to Sanskrit anupacita-śubha, 'virtue not accumulated,' and to the phrase śubhe ... anārabdhvā, 'not having undertaken virtue.' Describes the state of one who has not amassed a store of virtue.
Rendering Sanskrit kuśalasyānutpattiḥ, the non-arising or non-production of what is virtuous. Used both of the failure to produce virtue and of virtue that has not been generated.

dge ba mi zad bya ba'i phyir.gloss: in order not to exhaust virtue
